item.title: Daily Podcast 2026-09-16
item.description: The field used to rely on antibody‑based readouts to measure how well a drug degrades its target, but today’s work on MALT1 shows that a reagent‑free LC‑MS/MS assay can give absolute protein numbers and degradation percentages without any binding reagent, letting a lead compound be ranked by a DC50 of 5.2 nM in monkey splenocytes and an in vivo degradation of 77.9 % at a single dose. | In cirrhosis research, the assumption that liver disease mainly alters protein expression is being expanded by a glycomics study that profiled 46 serum and 23 IgG N‑glycan peaks using HILIC‑UPLC in just ten healthy controls, seventeen alcohol‑related cirrhosis patients, seven PSC cases and four HCC cases; they found specific increases in agalactosylated (GP4, GP5, GP6) and bisecting GlcNAc‑containing structures and decreases in sialylated traits, changes that correlated with MELD‑Na scores. | AI‑driven drug‑target interaction prediction is moving beyond static docking scores toward learning representations from raw sequences and structures; the review highlights how models now treat proteins and small molecules as graphs or language tokens, enabling the prediction of interactions for targets with no experimental structures—a shift that lets designers prioritize compounds for orphan receptors or splice variants where traditional docking would fail.
